names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 30 decembrie, «Sfânta Muceniță Anisia fecioara», with the rank words left off; the page the site keeps for her troparion names her «Sfânta Muceniță Anisia din Tesalonic».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 30 Δεκεμβρίου, «Αγία Ανυσία η Οσιομάρτυς από τη Θεσσαλονίκη», with the rank and the city left off.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (28 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 30 decembrie — «Sfânta Muceniță Anisia fecioara»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 30ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Αγία Ανυσία η Οσιομάρτυς από τη Θεσσαλονίκη»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 30 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps on the Romanian calendar, and the entry is the same woman: the rich orphan of Thessalonica run through the side by a soldier on her way to church. The page gives the year the folder had none for, in its head «(; - 298)» and in its text «έζησε στα χρόνια του αυτοκράτορα Διοκλητιανού (298 μ.Χ.)», and the `dates` object here is that and nothing more. It calls her Οσιομάρτυς where the folder's types are `martyr` and `virgin`; `venerable-martyr` is not added, because the page gives her no monastic state anywhere in its text and the Romanian calendar did not either — that is for the author. It names three places of relics, a part in the basilica of Saint Demetrius at Thessalonica and portions at the monastery of the Ascension at Proti of Serres and at Kykkos in Cyprus; none is drafted as a location. **It prints one apolytikion and says of it: «ΣΗΜΕΙΩΣΗ: Το Απολυτίκιο της είναι το ίδιο με αυτό της Οσίας Μελάνης (31 Δεκεμβρίου).»** The text names both women, «ω Ανυσία σεμνή» and «λαμπρυνθείσα Μελάνη», and ends in the dual, «και νυν ημίν ιλεούσθε» — so it is a hymn the two share and not another saint's proper hanging on her page, and it is taken with the page's own note recorded in its source. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (28 September 2026).

death.note: saint.gr's head for the entry gives «Αγια Ανυσια η Οσιομαρτυς Απο Τη Θεσσαλονικη (; - 298)», and its text «Η Αγία Ανυσία, έζησε στα χρόνια του αυτοκράτορα Διοκλητιανού (298 μ.Χ.)». No year of birth is given. doxologia.ro, which the folder follows, gave no year at all.

hymns.text: Οσίως ανύσασα, των αρετών την οδόν, τω Λόγω νενύμφευσαι, ω Ανυσία σεμνή, και χαίρουσα ήθλησας, αίγλη δε απαθείας, λαμπρυνθείσα Μελάνη, ήστραψας εν τω κόσμω, αρετών λαμπηδόνας, και νυν ημίν ιλεούσθε, Χριστόν τον Κύριον.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ήχος δ', Ταχύ προκατάλαβε — the only hymn on the page of «Αγία Ανυσία η Οσιομάρτυς από τη Θεσσαλονίκη». The page adds «ΣΗΜΕΙΩΣΗ: Το Απολυτίκιο της είναι το ίδιο με αυτό της Οσίας Μελάνης (31 Δεκεμβρίου)», and the text itself names both women and ends by asking them both together, so it is a hymn the two share and not another saint's proper.

english.text: Having holily accomplished the road of the virtues, you were betrothed to the Word, honoured Anysia, and you contended rejoicing; and you, Melania, made bright with the radiance of dispassion, flashed out upon the world the brilliance of the virtues. And now entreat Christ the Lord to be merciful to us.
